question: How do catastrophe bonds and reinsurance carry disaster risk?
answer: Alternative capital adds a funded layer to the reinsurance market. A sponsor transfers a defined risk to a special-purpose vehicle; investors fund collateral and receive a spread; a trigger can reduce principal or release collateral to the sponsor. The original insurer or public program normally remains the direct claimant-facing obligor. A hurricane, flood or earthquake is not itself the security trigger. For ordinary reinsurance the hub's rule is the same: ceded economics do not normally erase the original promise; cession ordinarily does not erase the direct insurer's policyholder obligation or prove that a recovery is due or collectible.

items.title: The special-purpose vehicle
items.sub: Alternative Risk Capital and Insurance-Linked Securities Control Map
items.text: Catastrophe bonds and collateralized reinsurance use special-purpose structures to hold eligible collateral against a defined risk period. Sidecars commonly accept a quota share of a sponsor's book. Bermuda's framework distinguishes special purpose insurers and collateralized insurers from ordinary commercial insurers.

items.title: Investor security, sponsor protection
items.sub: Alternative Risk Capital and Insurance-Linked Securities Control Map
items.text: Investor principal generally enters a collateral account invested under strict guidelines. Premium paid through the structure plus collateral investment earnings fund the note coupon. The sponsor receives protection under the risk-transfer agreement, while investors bear defined principal loss if the trigger is met. These are different records: offering, closing, funded collateral, risk period, event estimate, trigger determination, collateral release, note write-down and maturity. Announced issuance or target size does not prove a closed and fully funded placement.
kv: ALTERNATIVE_RISK_CAPITAL_AND_ILS_CONTROL_MAP_2026-10-01.md, section “3. The investor buys a security; the sponsor buys protection”

items.title: A public sponsor: the National Flood Insurance Program
items.sub: Alternative Risk Capital and Insurance-Linked Securities Control Map
items.text: FEMA buys both annual traditional reinsurance and multi-year catastrophe-bond protection for the National Flood Insurance Program. That changes the NFIP loss waterfall; it does not make investors the flood-policy issuer or eliminate the program's statutory borrowing and claims obligations.
kv: ALTERNATIVE_RISK_CAPITAL_AND_ILS_CONTROL_MAP_2026-10-01.md, section “5. Public sponsors can transfer public-program volatility”

items.title: Market size is provisional
items.sub: Alternative Risk Capital and Insurance-Linked Securities Control Map
items.text: Market estimates can describe issuance and outstanding capital, but definitions vary across catastrophe bonds, private ILS, sidecars and collateralized reinsurance. A vendor total is not a statutory census. The durable proof chain is deal-by-deal: sponsor, peril, geography, limit, attachment, trigger, collateral, term and observed recovery.

sections.title: Every box in the reinsurance lens

items.title: Primary insurer and policy
items.sub: Original promise · Creates the direct contractual promise
kv: Issues the policy and ordinarily remains responsible to the policyholder even when risk is ceded.
Controls underwriting, policy wording, premium, claim adjudication and payment subject to law and delegation.
A licence, form approval or quote is not a bound policy; reinsurance recovery is not the policyholder's ordinary direct claim.

items.title: Claim and coverage decision
items.sub: Original promise · Applies the promise to an occurred loss
kv: Records notice, proof of loss, coverage, exclusions, valuation, defence, appeal and settlement.
The policy and applicable law govern; administrator, insurer, adjuster, court or arbitrator may own successive decisions.
Event occurrence, insured loss estimate, claim submission, reserve, settlement and cash payment are separate states.

items.title: Ceding insurer
items.sub: Original promise · Keeps the direct promise while transferring defined economics
kv: Issues the policy, records gross obligations and seeks statutory credit and treaty recoveries.
Board, management, appointed actuary and domiciliary regulator govern the cession and remaining exposure.
Net reporting does not erase gross policy obligations or reveal every treaty term.

items.title: Reinsurance treaty
items.sub: Cession · Transfers defined economics from cedant to assuming entity
kv: Allocates specified premium, claims, reserves or catastrophe layers under treaty terms.
The treaty defines attachment, limits, exclusions, collateral, accounting, termination and recovery.
Cession ordinarily does not erase the direct insurer's policyholder obligation or prove that a recovery is due or collectible.

items.title: Asset-intensive reinsurer
items.sub: Cession · Assumes defined liabilities and asset economics
kv: Receives premium, reserves or investment economics under coinsurance, modified coinsurance, funds-withheld or related structures.
Treaty, domicile, collateral and investment terms determine actual control and capital treatment.

items.title: Reinsurance broker
items.sub: Cession · Designs and places capacity but does not normally bear it
kv: Structures submissions, obtains quotes, models towers and supports placement and claims communication.

items.title: Assuming reinsurer
items.sub: Cession · Bears the treaty layer on its own balance sheet
kv: Accepts premium and defined liability under proportional, excess, facultative or asset-intensive structures.

items.sub: Security & retrocession · Secures credit for reinsurance under defined control terms
kv: Supports cedant credit and access if the assuming entity fails or disputes arise.

items.title: Cat bond or collateralized risk capital
items.sub: Security & retrocession · Investor capital responds only to the named trigger
kv: Provides collateralized capacity through indemnity, industry-loss, parametric or modeled-loss triggers.

items.title: Retrocessionaire or sidecar
items.sub: Security & retrocession · Moves part of the assumed layer again
kv: Accepts a defined share of reinsurer exposure or capital participation.
Retrocession agreement, collateral, investor terms and commutation rights govern.

items.title: Actuarial control plane
items.sub: Supervision · Turns experience and assumptions into accountable records
kv: Links research, professional standards, company opinions and regulator-defined uses in rates, reserves and capital.

A study, model, exposure draft or signed opinion does not alone prove the final rate, reserve, approval or outcome.

items.sub: Supervision · Reserve and asset-intensive-reinsurance control records
kv: Places actuarial judgment and testing inside defined valuation and review structures.

items.sub: Supervision · Controls authorization, credit, capital and examinations

items.title: Reinsurance recovery
items.sub: Recovery & failure · A separate receivable and collection clock
kv: Records the cedant's treaty claim, allowed amount, offset, collateral access and cash collection.
Treaty language, claims cooperation, accounting and dispute terms govern the recovery.
A gross insured loss, ceded reserve or estimated recovery is not collected cash.

items.title: Life and health guaranty system
items.sub: Recovery & failure · State statutory protection after specified failure trigger
kv: Coordinates limited covered obligations after impairment or insolvency under state law.
Domiciliary receivership, guaranty statutes, limits, exclusions, assessments and transfer arrangements govern.
It is not pre-failure federal insurance, unlimited protection or a guarantee of every contract feature.

items.title: Recapture, commutation or resolution
items.sub: Recovery & failure · Changes exposure after stress, agreement or failure
kv: Returns liabilities, settles future treaty obligations or applies insolvency and collateral rights.
Treaty triggers, regulator approval, receivership law and negotiated terms determine the result.
A downgrade, review or concern does not prove recapture; a recapture does not by itself prove policyholder loss.

catalog_context.title: How insurers invest trillions, move risk and share losses with government
catalog_context.answer: U.S. insurance runs through many separate regulators, very large insurer balance sheets, reinsurance and public loss programs that together work as one system. Each authority, company, contract and payment still keeps its own legal identity and timing.
